messages:
elaine (eng-runtime): Heads up — CI microbench for PR 21345 is failing the perf threshold. Waterfall shows a clear spike centered at seqlen ~640 (512-1024 bucket). Delta: +22% latency vs baseline. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/int/21345/artifacts/waterfall.png

ci-bot: benchmark job #21345-microbench finished — threshold_diff=+22% (FAIL). Logs: https://ci.redwood/int/21345/artifacts/logs.txt

mike (eng-runtime): I skimmed the flamegraph — hot stack is in kernel_autoselect::choose_for_sequence_length, specifically fallback to dense-kernel for mid lengths. That method changed in merge 21200 (kernel heuristics refactor).

sam (eng-ml): KV cache hitrate for the microbench doesn't look worse (hit_pct ~ 87% same as baseline). This smells like scheduler/kernels not batching change.

anita (eng-sre): Is this reproducible locally? If so we can bisect pr range. If not, we should run the microbench in CI with verbose kernel selection logging.

mike (eng-runtime): Quick reproduce command I used locally: 
```
# run microbench docker image with sample traces
docker run --rm -v $PWD/traces:/traces ghcr.io/redwood/microbench:ci-21345 \
  --trace /traces/ops-mix-2026.json --seq-buckets 128,256,512,1024 --log-kernel-select
```
Flamegraph: hot frames -> kernel_autoselect::heuristic_score -> select_dense_kernel

elaine (eng-runtime): Nice. I pushed a debug CI variant that enables KERNEL_SELECT_VERBOSE env and uploaded logs to artifacts (link above). The waterfall + select trace shows the batcher picked dense-32 kernel at seqlen 640 which increased per-token cost.

mike (eng-runtime): Candidate culprit is commit abc1234 (part of merge 21200) where we changed fallback priority ordering for kernels with quantized paths. Reverting that commit locally removes the spike.

sam (eng-ml): I checked model traces: sequence length distribution didn't change, payload sizes same. So kernel chooser logic is likely the root cause.

anita (eng-sre): Proposed plan: 1) run automated bisect CI across merges 21190..21210 with kernel-select verbose enabled, 2) if bisect points to commit abc1234, open a revert PR and gate merge until fixed. Anyone object?

mike (eng-runtime): +1 from me. I'll prepare the bisect pipeline. Suggest we limit to 4 parallel jobs to avoid blowing quota.

elaine (eng-runtime): Created job: ci-bisect/21345-kernel-chooser with matrix of commits. Trigger: `/ci run bisect 21190..21210 --jobs 4 --env KERNEL_SELECT_VERBOSE=1`. Logs will dump into artifacts/bisect/<commit>/select.log

deploy-bot: Started pipeline ci-bisect/21345-kernel-chooser (4 jobs). Link: https://ci.redwood/int/bisect/21345

ci-bot: bisect job results: commit abc1234 reproduces +21% threshold diff. All other tested commits within noise.

mike (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Local revert test: `git revert abc1234 --no-edit && ./scripts/run_microbench.sh` -> baseline restored. Revert patch ready: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/21372

anita (eng-sre): Given this is blocking merge and affects PR/CI gates, I recommend temporary revert in main to avoid further rollouts. Who wants to approve revert PR?

elaine (eng-runtime): I'll approve and merge the revert after a quick smoke in staging. Plan: merge revert, run full microbench CI, unblock PR 21345.

sam (eng-ml): Also file a follow-up to rework kernel_autoselect heuristics with better cost-model checks (we should add a per-kernel expected-cost table indexed by seqlen).

mike (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll draft RFC/issue: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/7890 with perf regressions and a test harness to prevent this class of regression.

elaine (eng-runtime): Summary: bisect -> abc1234 blamed -> revert PR created and will be merged after staging smoke. Follow-up issue to improve heuristics + add regression tests. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

anita (eng-sre): Thanks all. Running staging smoke now.

mike (eng-runtime): thx 

sam (eng-ml): :thumbsup:
